name: Saratoga Spa State Park
blurb: A National Historic Landmark with mineral springs, Geyser Creek, classical bath houses, golf, walking trails, SPAC and the Gideon Putnam hotel — all in one 2,000+ acre park.

name: Congress Park
blurb: Downtown’s green heart: duck ponds, Congress Spring, the historic carousel and the Canfield Casino, steps from Broadway.

name: National Museum of Racing and Hall of Fame
blurb: Across from the track, with the Hall of Fame, Triple Crown trophies and the stories of the horses and jockeys that made the sport.

name: Yaddo Gardens
blurb: The rose garden and grounds of the famous artists’ retreat are open to the public. Quiet, fragrant and free.

name: Saratoga National Historical Park
blurb: The battlefield where the American victory in 1777 turned the Revolutionary War. Drive or bike the tour road, then climb the Saratoga Monument in nearby Victory.

name: Canfield Casino & Saratoga Springs History Museum
blurb: The 1870s gambling hall that drew the Gilded Age elite, now home to the city’s history museum.

name: Saratoga Automobile Museum
blurb: Rotating car exhibits housed in the park’s former bottling plant.

name: National Museum of Dance
blurb: The country’s museum and hall of fame for professional dance, in a former bath house.

name: High Rock Park
blurb: Home of High Rock Spring, the spring that started it all, plus the pavilion that hosts the farmers’ market.

name: Saratoga Race Course
blurb: Racing since 1863 and still the best summer day in America. Picnic in the backyard, watch morning workouts, stay for the Travers.

name: Saratoga Performing Arts Center (SPAC)
blurb: Summer home of the New York City Ballet and The Philadelphia Orchestra, plus the region’s big-name concerts. Lawn tickets and a picnic are the move.

name: Caffè Lena
blurb: Open since 1960 and one of the oldest continuously running folk coffeehouses in America — a young Bob Dylan played here. Intimate shows most nights.

name: Saratoga Lake
blurb: Boating, paddling, lakeside dining and some of the best rowing water in the country, a ten-minute drive from Broadway.

name: Saratoga Farmers’ Market
blurb: Local farms, bakers and makers under the High Rock pavilion. Check the market’s site for current days and the winter location.

name: Beekman Street Arts District
blurb: Galleries, studios and small restaurants in a historic neighborhood a few blocks west of Broadway.

name: Hattie’s
blurb: Southern fried chicken and soul food served in Saratoga since 1938. Expect a wait in August — worth it.

name: Mrs. London’s
blurb: The bakery-café for croissants, pastries and coffee on Broadway.

name: Esperanto
blurb: Late-night favorite famous for its doughboys, a Caroline Street rite of passage after the bars.

name: Druthers Brewing Company
blurb: Brewpub on Broadway with house beers and a big, easy menu.

name: Henry Street Taproom
blurb: Craft-beer bar with a serious tap list a block off Broadway.

name: The Adelphi Hotel
blurb: Grand Victorian hotel restored into Broadway’s boutique stay, with a bar that’s a destination on its own.

name: The Gideon Putnam
blurb: Classic 1930s hotel inside the state park — walk to SPAC, the baths and the trails.

name: Saratoga Hilton
blurb: Full-service hotel attached to the City Center, in the middle of downtown.

name: Saratoga Arms
blurb: A boutique inn in a historic Broadway mansion, an easy walk to the track.

name: Northshire Bookstore
blurb: A big, beloved independent bookstore with author events year-round.

name: Impressions of Saratoga
blurb: The place for Saratoga gifts, racing keepsakes and local goods.
